summary:
I wrote plan.md for both plots. Plot 0: Rockefeller Plaza street on the west and a 26 x 36 sunken well, using the lidar levels as given. Inside it are a 16 x 28 rink running north–south, glass-fronted restaurants lit warm under the north and south edges, umbrella terraces, and broad steps up to the gardens.
At the west end Prometheus is built in gold (gilded mount, a vertical ring, the figure flying horizontally with a glowing fire), set against a black granite wall with a gold zodiac ring and inscription. Around the well is a ring of 60 glowing white poles with mixed wool flags, all lit.
Plot 1: six turquoise-floored granite pools with bronze jets, flower and azalea planters, and walks that step up toward Fifth Avenue on three level terraces. Nothing was built or rendered yet; the toolkit doesn't know 1.21.1's `chain`, so swap it at delivery. Landscape kit with no buildings: a sunken ice-rink well with Prometheus against a dark zodiac wall, ringed by flags and glass-fronted restaurants. The Channel Gardens run east from it as six turquoise pools between flower planters.
elements.md and the PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS and PARTS sections are written. One palette fix: `polished_andesite_wall` doesn't exist in 1.21.1, so `andesite_wall` replaces it.

ground: parts/ground.mjs lays both plots' terrain to the lidar maps. It builds the gray_concrete road with curbs, crosswalks and a half-step ramp, andesite sidewalks, the granite-gridded promenade, and the well floor. It also does the restaurant floors and ceilings and the Channel Gardens terraces with half steps. make.sh shows 0 refused and 0 off-palette, and build.nbt is whole. I did not run `check`, `fit` or `render`.
polish: Well part: the well-edge ring (x20 and x45 at z10..45; z10 and z45 at x20..45) is left air for wellWall, except the basin floor at x20..22 z20..35. Step cells x42..47 z20..33 and cheek cells x42..45 z19/z34 are air for gardenSteps, and the rink ice cells are air.
Prometheus part: the wall footprint x18..19 z18..37 is air (all y), so the dark wall needs no overwrite.

Restaurants: I laid the floor y0, ceiling y4, and solid back and side walls. The glass-front lines z9 and z46 are air for glassFront. Their y4 head is the ground's smooth_stone, not the polished_andesite head the plan names.
Steps at x46..47 z19/34 are solid surface y4 so the planters stand on them; the cheek walls there are not built.

Half-step slabs between neighbouring map cells of the promenade and sidewalks were skipped; those cells snap to the mapped heights (steps of 1). Half steps exist only at the road ramp and the garden crosswalks.
Not yet inspected with render, check or fit.
Plot 1 z14..15 edge rows use the map heights, which differ slightly from the plan's three terraces at x75..76 and x99..100.

waste.what: Transcribed the 26x27 and 8x27 ground maps into code by hand and worked out the well, steps, wall and restaurant exclusion boxes
waste.cost: one big heredoc and several box computations
waste.tool: a groundFromMap(g, map, {surface(x,z), skip boxes}) helper that reads the brief's ground block and applies 2x2 cells, half steps and the outer-2 edge rule

waste.what: Decided which cells to leave as air for later parts by reasoning about each part's helper
waste.tool: a reserved-cells table in plan.json that ground helpers consult automatically

companions.task: Turn the lidar maps into exact 2x2-cell height arrays with half-step edge rows, and flag where the map disagrees with the plan's three snapped terraces.
Lay the granite band and grid patterns for the promenade, sidewalks and garden walks with proper border inside the parapets.

summary:
sunken well: Sunken well part built in parts/well.mjs: rink (packed ice, white rim with gates), Channel Gardens steps with cheeks, stair-head planters, north and south restaurant glass fronts with froglight bays, six umbrellas, retaining walls on the east and west sides, and the lip parapets.
make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt; the sunken well line shows 1226 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. mcd fit reports OK.
Elements P2 ticked in elements.md; a Notes line in plan.md records the planter shift and the wall layout.
polish: Planters moved to z16..18 and z35..37 (plan said z17..19 and z34..36), because the cheek walls at z19 and z34 take those cells; recorded in plan.md Notes.
No retaining walls on the north and south edges (z10 and z45 rows): those are the terrace edges under the restaurant glass at z9 and z46, so the ring cells stay air as the ground part left them.
The restaurant glass reads poorly in the zoom render from the south; the piers and panes may need a check against the concept at the lighting pass.
The whole-build walkable check reports false (narrowest 0 along x). That comes from the ground and well layout, not this part alone, and is for the integrator.
Prometheus basin, gold figure, flags, gardens and lamps are not in this part.

waste.what: Worked out the rink, rim gap, planter and terrace coordinates by hand and checked them against the plan's collisions (cheek walls vs planters, terrace floor vs north wall).
waste.cost: About 6 minutes of reasoning; no retries of the build.
waste.tool: A plan-collision check in the build library: a 'would overlap' report for each element's footprint against the earlier elements' cells, before the part is written.

waste.what: Rink rim and gap arguments were given as [x0,z0,x1,z1] boxes by hand, so each gap's edge cells had to be recomputed.
waste.cost: Four gap boxes worked out by hand.
waste.tool: rinkRim taking named gaps (gate, terrace, dark rim) from base.mjs constants, not raw boxes.

waste.what: Visual check of the restaurant glass was done by eye from zoom tiles; glass and piers do not read clearly from the south.
waste.cost: Two zoom renders and a read of each.
waste.tool: A per-face glazing report from mcd (glass cells per bay, connection states) to confirm the front without a render.

companions.task: Lay the retaining walls and the granite steps and check the cheek walls flush with each tread, including the x45 wall under the steps.
Fit the restaurant glass fronts (piers, panes, the double birch doors at x32..33) and check the connection states along each bay.
Plant the stair-head and terrace planters and check the planter curbs against the promenade ground.

summary:
prometheus: Prometheus part built in parts/prometheus.mjs: dark wall x18..19 z18..37 with zodiac ring, inscription bands, basin water and cascades, and the gilded figure with mount and gold ring (vocab prometheus() helper at x20, z24), plus four wall-top lanterns.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; prometheus line shows 610 placed, no off-palette blocks, and 48 refused writes (the basin floor at y0, which the ground part's smooth_stone already holds).
The basin floor stays smooth_stone instead of polished_blackstone, three ring cells hang by one face, and the zodiac inscription is alternating bands rather than lettering.
polish: Basin floor y0 x20..22 z20..35 is the ground part's smooth_stone, not polished_blackstone: runParts locks it (48 refused writes). The sunken-well part should lay the floor if it owns it.
mcd check reports 3 gold ring cells that touch the build on one face only (x21 y3 z25, y3 z30, y8 z25). A one-thick diagonal circle can't avoid this without thickening the ring.

Basin is not ticked in elements.md: the cascades and water sources are built, but the floor/rim item is incomplete. The basin rim at x23 (y1 blackstone, y2 slab) is also not checked against the well's walls.
Inscription is alternating raw_gold/blackstone bricks as the spec says, not lettering; it reads as a gold band at distance, not as words.
Figure occupies z24..31 (the helper's footprint), not the plan's z25..30 body plus arm z30..31. The ring is centred correctly at (y5.5, z27.5).
The wall-top lanterns at x18 y11 z18/23/32/37 sit in the spec but may collide with the lighting part's writes; those will be refused if lights runs later.

waste.what: Worked out the gold ring's cell layout by hand, then printed the x=21 plane with a throwaway script to find which cells were orphaned and where to add connectors.
waste.cost: about 3 script runs and 2 rebuilds; four connector cells placed by coordinate guess, which created three new orphans
waste.tool: mcd check should print an ASCII slice of a plane around each orphan (e.g. `mcd slice build.nbt --plane x=21 --y 0..10 --z 22..33`), so connector placement is one look instead of trial and error.

waste.what: Ticked elements.md rows by line number after two failed sed attempts, and appended a Notes line to plan.md by hand.
waste.tool: a `mcd tick <elements.md> --part P3 --built` command, or a plan helper that writes the checklist and notes from the part's manifest.

waste.what: Confirmed by reading the refusal list that the basin floor clash is the only write conflict, by printing the refusedAt entries and grouping them by y.
waste.tool: parts-report.json could group refusals by (y, old block, new block) so the lock conflict is visible in the make.sh line itself.

companions.task: Model the figure's gold modelling and the ring: which cells are raw_gold versus gold_block, and whether the ring's diagonal steps should be thickened or left as a fine wire.
Lay out the inscription band as real letters, cut into the dark wall face, instead of alternating gold and blackstone bricks.
Lay the polished_blackstone basin floor and the rim course with the well's wall, which the ground part's smooth_stone blocks.
Confirm the four wall-top lanterns at x18 y11 and whether the lights part is also placing lanterns there, so they are not doubled or refused.

summary:
flags: Flags part built in parts/flags.mjs: 60 white end_rod flagpoles on the north (z7), south (z48), west (x17) and east (x48) promenade lines, one every 2 blocks, each with a 2x2 mixed-colour wool flag at y10..11 pointing out from the well.
Poles that stand on ground reading 5 at y5 (west strip x17 z8..34 and z38, north pole x20 z7) start at y6, so they are 6 tall; this is noted in plan.md Notes.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; the flags line shows 644 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; zoomed render reads as the flag ring.
polish: Poles at x17 z8..34, z38 and x20 z7 are 6 tall (y6..11), not the 7 the plan gives, because the ground there is at 5; a fix would mean lowering the ground map or raising the flags, which is not my part.
Flag ring is at the promenade edge only; the flags were not checked against the lighting part's lanterns (lights.mjs is still a stub).

waste.what: Silent refusals: flagPole's internal put() refuses cells that are not air (the y5 cell where ground reads 5), but the refusals never reach runParts' report, so the flags line showed 0 refused. I only found the 16 short poles by scanning the built nbt column by column.
waste.cost: about 4 scan runs and one wrong fix attempt before the root cause was clear
waste.tool: flagPole (and the other vocab helpers) should return or surface res.refused into runParts' per-part report, and a helper like surfaceTop(g, x, z) should give the first air y above the ground so each pole base is chosen without hand checks.

waste.what: Per-column pole census: I wrote /tmp/flagcheck.mjs to count end_rod cells per column, because mcd info only gives totals (404 end_rod vs 420 expected).
waste.tool: mcd info --column-census or mcd check listing partial poles/columns by block id would have shown it directly.

waste.what: Coordinates for the four flag lines were worked out by hand from plan.md (ranges with steps of 2 and the two east segments).
waste.tool: A plan-table reader that turns the 'Poles at' tables into [x,z] lists would have removed the transcription step.

companions.task: Pick the mixed national-style colour pairs for the 14 flags per side, so the ring reads as a set of nations' flags rather than one repeated colour.
Check that the pole bases sit on the real promenade surface and that the 6-tall poles on the west strip are either lowered into the ground map or lengthened to the planned 7.
Check where the lanterns on the parapets and the rink rim meet the flagpole ring, so the flags are lit at dusk with no dark cells beside them.

summary:
channel gardens: Plot 1 channel gardens built in parts/gardens.mjs: six pools (rims, water, a copper jet at each east end), plantBed planters on both sides of each pool, and 24 andesite-stair benches on the walks at z3/z12.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the gardens line shows 378 placed and no off-palette blocks, and info confirms 6 waxed_exposed_copper jets and 24 polished_andesite_stairs.
The six prismarine_bricks pool floors are REFUSED (144 cells): the ground part already laid smooth_stone at y g there, and runParts locks it. Noted in plan.md Notes; the ground part or the plan must resolve it.
polish: Pool floors (prismarine_bricks at y g, z 6..9 across all six pools) are refused: the ground part's smooth_stone surface holds those cells. Fix in the ground part (leave the pool floor cells for the pool) or accept smooth_stone as the pool bottom in plan.md; elements.md 'Six granite pools' left unticked for this reason.
plantBed's flora list has no peony or rose_bush (2-high), so the requested peonies/roses are missing from the planters.
Jets are at z 7 only (one per pool); the water source at g+2 sits on the copper figure and does not run down the pool as the brief describes.

waste.what: Found the pool-floor conflict only by running make.sh: the ground's smooth_stone at y g on the pool cells was not checked against the pool spec before writing.
waste.cost: one full build run plus a re-read of the ground map (about 1 retry)
waste.tool: A check (build library or mcd check --site) that lists each part's planned cells against the earlier parts' filled cells before a build, so an overlap shows up at plan time.

waste.what: Worked out the 2-deep planter edge rule by hand: plantBed treats every cell on z0/z1 as curb, so the pool side had to be opened with open:['south'|'north'] to get soil up to the pool rim.
waste.cost: a few reasoning passes over the helper's source
waste.tool: plantBed option naming the curb sides as a single argument (e.g. curb:['walk','ends']) plus a note in the vocab comment that a 2-wide bed is all curb unless opened.

waste.what: Bench x positions (x0+1 and x1-1 per segment) and the jet's z row chosen by hand from the plan's prose.
waste.tool: A plan table of bench and jet cells per segment (like POOLS in vocab/base.mjs) so the part can read them instead of re-deriving them.

waste.what: Checked the rendered planters and pools by a single zoom view and by eye, not by a measured check.
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a fixed side and a per-part census of the expected cell types (pool water 48, copper 6, stairs 24) asserted in make.sh.

companions.task: Lay the six prismarine_bricks pool floors, flush with the ground surface, so the turquoise floor of the photo reads through the water.
Cast and set the six bronze jet figures in the pool ends, with the water sources feeding them.
Choose the planter mix (peonies and roses in addition to the tulips and azaleas) and its seasonal rhythm along each bed.

summary:
lighting: parts/lights.mjs places all 24 lamp posts (10 on plot 0 at x2/x14 z5..45, 14 on plot 1 at z2/z13) with lanterns on top, 120 blocks, none refused. Plot 1's x74 lamps moved to x72 because x74 sits in the step-up crosswalk's half-step slab.
It also reports walkable cells under light 8 and at light 0 after the lamps go in. make.sh finishes and writes a whole build.nbt. The light counts only mean something after the other parts merge.
polish: Dark check is not final: in this copy the other parts are stubs, so the report counts 2381 cells under light 8 and 977 at light 0. The well's rim and parapet lanterns, the flag end rods and the Prometheus lanterns must be merged before the count means anything.

South promenade (z 46..53) and the west sidewalk have no lamp of their own; they rely on the parapets and flag poles. Re-run the report after merge and add a lamp at the south promenade if cells stay at light 0.
Plot 1 lamps at x66, x82, x90 and x98 stand in the crosswalks, which are 2 wide, so each leaves one column open. Flagged in plan.md Notes; the owner should confirm.
No rendered check of the lamps against the concept yet; the street tile shows them only as small dark posts at this scale.

waste.what: Looked up the surface height under each of the 10 plot 0 lamp posts by counting rows and columns of the GROUND map by hand.
waste.cost: about 10 lookups and two recounts of the map rows
waste.tool: A helper such as surfaceAt(g, x, z) that reads the top solid block from the built grid, or a lampPost option that takes the ground map and the cell instead of a base y.

waste.what: Worked out the dark-cell check myself: the nearest light per walkable cell (level = 15 minus Manhattan distance) and two thresholds, under 8 and 0, in lights.mjs.
waste.cost: about 60 lines of JS and two runs of make.sh
waste.tool: `mcd light build.nbt --y <feet>` should report the count of cells under 8 and at 0 as numbers, not only the level map. Its open-air reach rule also needs to match the lamplighter's aim.

waste.what: Found the lamp at x74 collides with the ground's half-step by trial: one post cell refused, the rest placed and floating, after a full make.sh run.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and a fix
waste.tool: A check in runParts or the palette step that flags a lamp or post whose base cell is not solid, or a refused count on the post's first block that also aborts the stack.

waste.what: The result() helper returns a placed count, but refused is a list of cells, so the part's return value had to be read by hand.
waste.cost: one TypeError on the first run
waste.tool: Make the vocab helpers return the same shape, such as placed as a count and refused as a list, documented in the helper comment.

companions.task: Review the dusk light plan: which cells are dark after the merge, where the south promenade and west sidewalk need an extra lamp, and whether the crosswalk lamps at x66 to x98 should move off the crossing.
Set the lamp posts into the crosswalk and walk layouts so they sit off the crossing path, and check the post height against the parapet lanterns.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
